prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Context: FAA NextGen aims to raise National Airspace System (NAS) capacity; en route weather causes ~70% of US delays. System: NASA Airspace Technology Demonstrations 3 (ATD-3), ground/aircraft decision aids for weather-avoidance routing, TMI response, en route/arrival metering. Subset: NASA Dynamic Weather Routes (DWR), cruise phase, using existing weather/airspace/traffic data and ATM automation; extends NASA Direct-To tool; constraints modeled as polygons. Current system: FAA traffic managers set static Flow Constrained Areas (FCA) and Severe Weather Avoidance Plans (SWAP, aka Playbook routes) 2-8 h ahead; airline flight dispatchers file flight plans >=45 min before push-back; Collaborative Trajectory Options Program (CTOP) strategic only; controllers, dispatchers, flight crews request amendments manually; crews use flight management systems and limited-range on-board weather radar. Gap: no automation flags expired constraints or savings. DWR: ground automation continuously analyzing in-flight aircraft at/above 10,000 ft using radar track and flight plan updates; seeks time/fuel-saving weather-avoidance or wind-favorable direct-to corrections, considering convective weather, traffic conflicts, sector congestion, Special Use Airspace (SUA), FAA restrictions. Reference direct route from Maneuver Start Point (MSP) to Return Capture Fix (RCF; downstream fix where route rejoins flight plan). MSP default 5 min ahead (accepted in American Airlines trials) or, for climbing flights, point reaching high-altitude airspace (FL240 for Fort Worth Center, ZFW); models coordination delay; all advisories start with default MSP; user can drag MSP in trial planning; MSP snaps to flight plan fix within 10 nmi. Default RCF via Center-unique limit region: ZFW limit rectangle ~200 nmi beyond boundary; RCF = last flight plan fix inside region, or last fix before arrival STAR if landing inside. Alternative: convex limit polygon from historical direct clearances, implemented in NAS Constraint Evaluation and Notification Tool (NASCENT), the Future ATM Concept Evaluation Tool (FACET) implementation of DWR; city-pair RCF possible. If wind-corrected savings >= user minimum (default 5 min), route probed; 1-2 auxiliary waypoints added to avoid weather (optionally traffic) giving minimum-delay route; optional snap-to named fix; solutions posted to DWR alert list. Congested

Document units:
U0090: If a route correction is found that can save the user-defined minimum time or more relative to the current flight plan, the flight is posted to a list displayed to an FAA traffic manager or to an airline ATC coordinator (see Figure 4).
U0091: The user is provided with a DWR reroute advisory for each flight that fits the weather-avoidance and time-savings criteria, and can select and modify the new route prior to clearing the aircraft to fly it.
U0092: Auxiliary waypoints are defined using fix-radial-distance format, and a “snap-to” option utilizes nearby named fixes for ease of use in today’s operations (see Figure 1).
U0093: DWR route correction advisories are posted to a DWR flight list as shown in Figure 4.
U0094: The list, ordered by potential flight-time savings, includes all flights for which a route correction advisory has been identified, and for which the user has responsibility, and is prominently displayed on the user’s traffic display.
U0095: Each list element includes the flight ID (call sign), the estimated flight-time savings, and other relevant summary information such as city pair, aircraft type, route correction summary (e.g., RCF and number of inserted auxiliary waypoints), and summary information pertinent to the status of traffic conflicts, traffic congestion, and any FAA routing restrictions.
U0096: Any given flight for which a route correction advisory has been identified at the last trajectory update remains on the flight list.
U0097: Figure 4: DWR List Also shown for each list entry there are traffic (TR), sector load (SC), and weather (WX) conflict status indicators.
U0098: A number in the TR column indicates minutes to a detected conflict on the DWR route.
U0099: An “SC” entry in the SC column is color coded yellow or red indicating the DWR route is predicted to pass through a sector in yellow or red congestion status.
U0100: An R in the TMI columns indicates that the flight is currently impacted by an active Route TMI.
U0101: Figure 5 shows the display interface for DWR.
U0102: The big window on the left is the Plan-view Graphical User Interface.
U0103: In this window, a flight’s ‘Current flight plan route’ is shown in a solid-white line and represents a SWAP/Playbook route.
